General Concepts
================


Serializer vs Signer
--------------------

ItsDangerous provides two levels of data handling. The :doc:`/signer` is
the basic system that signs a given ``bytes`` value based on the given
signing parameters. The :doc:`/serializer` wraps a signer to enable
serializing and signing other data besides ``bytes``.

Typically, you'll want to use a serializer, not a signer. You can
configure the signing parameters through the serializer, and even
provide fallback signers to upgrade old tokens to new parameters.


The Secret Key
--------------

Signatures are secured by the ``secret_key``. Typically one secret key
is used with all signers, and the salt is used to distinguish different
contexts. Changing the secret key will invalidate existing tokens.

It should be a long random string of bytes. This value must be kept
secret and should not be saved in source code or committed to version
control. If an attacker learns the secret key, they can change and
resign data to look valid. If you suspect this happened, change the
secret key to invalidate existing tokens.

One way to keep the secret key separate is to read it from an
environment variable. When deploying for the first time, generate a key
and set the environment variable when running the application. All
process managers (like systemd) and hosting services have a way to
specify environment variables.

.. code-block:: python

    import os
    from itsdangerous.serializer import Serializer
    SECRET_KEY = os.environ.get("SECRET_KEY")
    s = Serializer(SECRET_KEY)

.. code-block:: text

    $ export SECRET_KEY="base64 encoded random bytes"
    $ python application.py

One way to generate a key is to use :func:`os.urandom`.

.. code-block:: text

    $ python3 -c 'import os; print(os.urandom(16).hex())'


The Salt
--------

The salt is combined with the secret key to derive a unique key for
distinguishing different contexts. Unlike the secret key, the salt
doesn't have to be random, and can be saved in code. It only has to be
unique between contexts, not private.

For example, you want to email activation links to activate user
accounts, and upgrade links to upgrade users to a paid accounts. If all
you sign is the user id, and you don't use different salts, a user could
reuse the token from the activation link to upgrade the account. If you
use different salts, the signatures will be different and will not be
valid in the other context.

.. code-block:: python

    from itsdangerous.url_safe import URLSafeSerializer

    s1 = URLSafeSerializer("secret-key", salt="activate")
    s1.dumps(42)
    'NDI.MHQqszw6Wc81wOBQszCrEE_RlzY'

    s2 = URLSafeSerializer("secret-key", salt="upgrade")
    s2.dumps(42)
    'NDI.c0MpsD6gzpilOAeUPra3NShPXsE'

The second serializer can't load data dumped with the first because the
salts differ.

.. code-block:: python

    s2.loads(s1.dumps(42))
    Traceback (most recent call last):
      ...
    BadSignature: Signature does not match

Only the serializer with the same salt can load the data.

.. code-block:: python

    s2.loads(s2.dumps(42))
    42


Key Rotation
------------

Key rotation can provide an extra layer of mitigation against an
attacker discovering a secret key. A rotation system will keep a list of
valid keys, generating a new key and removing the oldest key
periodically. If it takes four weeks for an attacker to crack a key, but
the key is rotated out after three weeks, they will not be able to use
any keys they crack. However, if a user doesn't refresh their token
within three weeks it will be invalid too.

The system that generates and maintains this list is outside the scope
of ItsDangerous, but ItsDangerous does support validating against a list
of keys.

Instead of passing a single key, you can pass a list of keys, oldest to
newest. When signing the last (newest) key will be used, and when
validating each key will be tried from newest to oldest before raising
a validation error.

.. code-block:: python

    SECRET_KEYS = ["2b9cd98e", "169d7886", "b6af09f5"]

    # sign some data with the latest key
    s = Serializer(SECRET_KEYS)
    t = s.dumps({"id": 42})

    # rotate a new key in and the oldest key out
    SECRET_KEYS.append("cf9b3588")
    del SECRET_KEYS[0]

    s = Serializer(SECRET_KEYS)
    s.loads(t)  # valid even though it was signed with a previous key


Digest Method Security
----------------------

A signer is configured with a ``digest_method``, a hash function that
is used as an intermediate step when generating the HMAC signature. The
default method is :func:`hashlib.sha1`. Occasionally, users are
concerned about this default because they have heard about hash
collisions with SHA-1.

When used as the intermediate, iterated step in HMAC, SHA-1 is not
insecure. In fact, even MD5 is still secure in HMAC. The security of the
hash alone doesn't apply when used in HMAC.

If a project considers SHA-1 a risk anyway, they can configure the
signer with a different digest method such as :func:`hashlib.sha512`.
A fallback signer for SHA-1 can be configured so that old tokens will be
upgraded. SHA-512 produces a longer hash, so tokens will take up more
space, which is relevant in cookies and URLs.

    s2.loads(s1.dumps(42))
    Traceback (most recent call last):
      ...
    BadSignature: Signature does not match

Only the serializer with the same salt can load the data.

.. code-block:: python

    s2.loads(s2.dumps(42))
    42


Key Rotation
------------

Key rotation can provide an extra layer of mitigation against an
attacker discovering a secret key. A rotation system will keep a list of
valid keys, generating a new key and removing the oldest key
periodically. If it takes four weeks for an attacker to crack a key, but
the key is rotated out after three weeks, they will not be able to use
any keys they crack. However, if a user doesn't refresh their token
within three weeks it will be invalid too.

The system that generates and maintains this list is outside the scope
of ItsDangerous, but ItsDangerous does support validating against a list
of keys.

Instead of passing a single key, you can pass a list of keys, oldest to
newest. When signing the last (newest) key will be used, and when
validating each key will be tried from newest to oldest before raising
a validation error.

.. code-block:: python

    SECRET_KEYS = ["2b9cd98e", "169d7886", "b6af09f5"]

    # sign some data with the latest key
    s = Serializer(SECRET_KEYS)
    t = s.dumps({"id": 42})

    # rotate a new key in and the oldest key out
    SECRET_KEYS.append("cf9b3588")
    del SECRET_KEYS[0]

    s = Serializer(SECRET_KEYS)
    s.loads(t)  # valid even though it was signed with a previous key


Digest Method Security
----------------------

A signer is configured with a ``digest_method``, a hash function that
is used as an intermediate step when generating the HMAC signature. The
default method is :func:`hashlib.sha1`. Occasionally, users are
concerned about this default because they have heard about hash
collisions with SHA-1.

When used as the intermediate, iterated step in HMAC, SHA-1 is not
insecure. In fact, even MD5 is still secure in HMAC. The security of the
hash alone doesn't apply when used in HMAC.

If a project considers SHA-1 a risk anyway, they can configure the
signer with a different digest method such as :func:`hashlib.sha512`.
A fallback signer for SHA-1 can be configured so that old tokens will be
upgraded. SHA-512 produces a longer hash, so tokens will take up more
space, which is relevant in cookies and URLs.

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import os
from datetime import datetime
from datetime import timedelta
from datetime import timezone

import pytest
from freezegun import freeze_time

from itsdangerous import BadHeader
from itsdangerous import BadSignature
from itsdangerous import Key
from itsdangerous import KeyExpired
from itsdangerous import KeyRevoked
from itsdangerous import KeyRing
from itsdangerous import Signer
from itsdangerous import TimestampSigner
from itsdangerous import UnknownKeyIdentifier
from itsdangerous import URLSafeTimedSerializer


def make_secret() -> bytes:
    return os.urandom(32)


def make_ring(*, revoked: bool = False) -> KeyRing:
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    return KeyRing(
        [
            Key.verification_only(
                make_secret(),
                "old",
                expires_at=now + timedelta(days=30),
                revoked=revoked,
            ),
            Key.signing(make_secret(), "current"),
        ]
    )


class TestVersionedEnvelope:
    def test_signer_round_trip_and_header(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        signer = Signer(key_ring=ring)

        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")

        assert signed.startswith(b"v1-current.")
        assert signer.unsign(signed) == b"payload"

    def test_timestamped_round_trip(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        signer = TimestampSigner(key_ring=ring)
        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")

        assert signed.startswith(b"v1-current.")
        assert signer.unsign(signed, max_age=10) == b"payload"

    def test_url_safe_full_stack_with_compression_and_max_age(self):
        serializer = URLSafeTimedSerializer(key_ring=make_ring())
        value = {"message": "x" * 1000}
        token = serializer.dumps(value)

        assert token.startswith("v1-current.")
        assert all(char.isascii() and char not in "?#" for char in token)
        assert serializer.loads(token, max_age=10) == value

    def test_kid_selects_exact_key(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        signer = Signer(key_ring=ring)
        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")

        class OneKeyAlgorithm:
            calls = 0

            def get_signature(self, key, value):
                type(self).calls += 1
                return hashlib.sha256(key + value).digest()

            def verify_signature(self, key, value, sig):
                return self.get_signature(key, value) == sig

        verifier = Signer(
            key_ring=ring,
            algorithm=OneKeyAlgorithm(),
            digest_method=hashlib.sha256,
        )

        with pytest.raises(BadSignature):
            verifier.unsign(signed)

        assert OneKeyAlgorithm.calls == 1

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("position", (0, 1))
    def test_tampered_kid_fails(self, position):
        signer = Signer(key_ring=make_ring())
        signed = bytearray(signer.sign(b"payload"))
        signed[position] = ord("x")

        with pytest.raises((BadHeader, BadSignature)):
            signer.unsign(bytes(signed))

    def test_version_downgrade_fails(self):
        signer = Signer(key_ring=make_ring())
        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")
        downgraded = signed.replace(b"v1-", b"v0-", 1)

        with pytest.raises(BadSignature):
            signer.unsign(downgraded)

    def test_unknown_kid_is_header_error(self):
        signer = Signer(key_ring=make_ring())
        signed = signer.sign(b"payload").replace(b"v1-current", b"v1-missing", 1)

        with pytest.raises(UnknownKeyIdentifier) as exc_info:
            signer.unsign(signed)

        assert isinstance(exc_info.value, BadHeader)

    def test_invalid_signature_encoding(self):
        signer = Signer(key_ring=make_ring())
        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")
        value, _sig = signed.rsplit(b".", 1)

        with pytest.raises(BadSignature):
            signer.unsign(value + b".bad/sig")

    def test_kid_cannot_contain_separator(self):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            Key(make_secret(), "bad.kid")

    def test_legacy_token_remains_valid(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        old_signer = Signer(ring.secret_keys)
        old_signed = self._legacy_sign(old_signer, b"payload")

        assert not old_signed.startswith(b"v1-")
        assert Signer(key_ring=ring).unsign(old_signed) == b"payload"

    def test_legacy_looking_token_is_not_confused_with_new_format(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        old_signer = Signer(ring.secret_keys)
        old_signed = self._legacy_sign(old_signer, b"v1-current.actual-payload")

        assert Signer(key_ring=ring).unsign(old_signed) == b"v1-current.actual-payload"

    @staticmethod
    def _legacy_sign(signer: Signer, value: bytes) -> bytes:
        key = signer.derive_key(signer.secret_keys[-1])
        signature = signer.algorithm.get_signature(key, value)
        from itsdangerous.encoding import base64_encode

        return value + signer.sep + base64_encode(signature)


class TestKeyLifecycle:
    def test_expired_key_is_rejected_with_distinct_error(self):
        now = datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=timezone.utc)
        ring = KeyRing(
            [
                Key.verification_only(
                    make_secret(), "old", expires_at=now - timedelta(seconds=1)
                ),
                Key.signing(make_secret(), "current"),
            ]
        )
        old_ring = KeyRing(
            [
                Key.signing(ring.keys[0].secret_key, "old"),
                Key.verification_only(ring.keys[1].secret_key, "current"),
            ]
        )
        token = Signer(key_ring=old_ring).sign(b"payload")

        with freeze_time(now):
            with pytest.raises(KeyExpired):
                Signer(key_ring=ring).unsign(token)

    def test_revoked_key_is_rejected_with_distinct_error(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        active_ring = KeyRing(
            [
                Key.signing(ring.keys[0].secret_key, "old"),
                Key.verification_only(ring.keys[1].secret_key, "current"),
            ]
        )
        token = Signer(key_ring=active_ring).sign(b"payload")
        revoked_ring = make_ring(revoked=True)

        with pytest.raises(KeyRevoked):
            Signer(key_ring=revoked_ring).unsign(token)

    def test_verification_only_key_cannot_sign(self):
        ring = KeyRing(
            [
                Key.verification_only(make_secret(), "old"),
                Key(make_secret(), "current", can_sign=False, can_verify=True),
            ]
        )

        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            Signer(key_ring=ring)

    def test_expiration_requires_timezone(self):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            Key(make_secret(), "kid", expires_at=datetime(2026, 1, 1))

    def test_duplicate_kid_is_rejected(self):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            KeyRing(
                [
                    Key.verification_only(make_secret(), "same"),
                    Key.signing(make_secret(), "same"),
                ]
            )

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import os
from datetime import datetime
from datetime import timedelta
from datetime import timezone

import pytest
from freezegun import freeze_time

from itsdangerous import BadHeader
from itsdangerous import BadSignature
from itsdangerous import Key
from itsdangerous import KeyExpired
from itsdangerous import KeyRevoked
from itsdangerous import KeyRing
from itsdangerous import Signer
from itsdangerous import TimestampSigner
from itsdangerous import UnknownKeyIdentifier
from itsdangerous import URLSafeTimedSerializer


def make_secret() -> bytes:
    return os.urandom(32)


def make_ring(*, revoked: bool = False) -> KeyRing:
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    return KeyRing(
        [
            Key.verification_only(
                make_secret(),
                "old",
                expires_at=now + timedelta(days=30),
                revoked=revoked,
            ),
            Key.signing(make_secret(), "current"),
        ]
    )


class TestVersionedEnvelope:
    def test_signer_round_trip_and_header(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        signer = Signer(key_ring=ring)

        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")

        assert signed.startswith(b"v1-current.")
        assert signer.unsign(signed) == b"payload"

    def test_timestamped_round_trip(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        signer = TimestampSigner(key_ring=ring)
        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")

        assert signed.startswith(b"v1-current.")
        assert signer.unsign(signed, max_age=10) == b"payload"

    def test_url_safe_full_stack_with_compression_and_max_age(self):
        serializer = URLSafeTimedSerializer(key_ring=make_ring())
        value = {"message": "x" * 1000}
        token = serializer.dumps(value)

        assert token.startswith("v1-current.")
        assert all(char.isascii() and char not in "?#" for char in token)
        assert serializer.loads(token, max_age=10) == value

    def test_kid_selects_exact_key(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        signer = Signer(key_ring=ring)
        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")

        class OneKeyAlgorithm:
            calls = 0
            hmac_algorithm = signer.algorithm

            def get_signature(self, key, value):
                type(self).calls += 1
                return self.hmac_algorithm.get_signature(key, value)

            def verify_signature(self, key, value, sig):
                return self.hmac_algorithm.verify_signature(key, value, sig)

        verifier = Signer(key_ring=ring, algorithm=OneKeyAlgorithm())

        assert verifier.unsign(signed) == b"payload"

        assert OneKeyAlgorithm.calls == 1

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("position", (0, 1))
    def test_tampered_kid_fails(self, position):
        signer = Signer(key_ring=make_ring())
        signed = bytearray(signer.sign(b"payload"))
        signed[position] = ord("x")

        with pytest.raises((BadHeader, BadSignature)):
            signer.unsign(bytes(signed))

    def test_version_downgrade_fails(self):
        signer = Signer(key_ring=make_ring())
        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")
        downgraded = signed.replace(b"v1-", b"v0-", 1)

        with pytest.raises(BadSignature):
            signer.unsign(downgraded)

    def test_unknown_kid_is_header_error(self):
        signer = Signer(key_ring=make_ring())
        signed = signer.sign(b"payload").replace(b"v1-current", b"v1-missing", 1)

        with pytest.raises(UnknownKeyIdentifier) as exc_info:
            signer.unsign(signed)

        assert isinstance(exc_info.value, BadHeader)

    def test_invalid_signature_encoding(self):
        signer = Signer(key_ring=make_ring())
        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")
        value, _sig = signed.rsplit(b".", 1)

        with pytest.raises(BadSignature):
            signer.unsign(value + b".bad/sig")

    def test_kid_cannot_contain_separator(self):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            Key(make_secret(), "bad.kid")

    def test_legacy_token_remains_valid(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        old_signer = Signer(ring.secret_keys)
        old_signed = self._legacy_sign(old_signer, b"payload")

        assert not old_signed.startswith(b"v1-")
        assert Signer(key_ring=ring).unsign(old_signed) == b"payload"

    def test_legacy_looking_token_is_not_confused_with_new_format(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        old_signer = Signer(ring.secret_keys)
        old_signed = self._legacy_sign(old_signer, b"v1-current.actual-payload")

        assert Signer(key_ring=ring).unsign(old_signed) == b"v1-current.actual-payload"

    @staticmethod
    def _legacy_sign(signer: Signer, value: bytes) -> bytes:
        key = signer.derive_key(signer.secret_keys[-1])
        signature = signer.algorithm.get_signature(key, value)
        from itsdangerous.encoding import base64_encode

        return value + signer.sep + base64_encode(signature)


class TestKeyLifecycle:

from __future__ import annotations

import collections.abc as cabc
import hashlib
import hmac
import re
import typing as t
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime

from .encoding import want_bytes
from .exc import KeyExpired
from .exc import KeyRevoked
from .exc import KeySigningError
from .exc import KeyStatusError
from .exc import UnknownKeyIdentifier

if t.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from .signer import _SecretKeyInput

# Key identifiers are public. Restricting them to the URL-safe base64
# alphabet without padding means they can never contain the envelope
# separator and need no percent-encoding in URLs or HTTP headers.
_KID_RE = re.compile(rb"[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128}\Z")


def validate_kid(kid: str) -> bytes:
    """Validate and encode a public key identifier."""
    value = want_bytes(kid, encoding="ascii")

    if _KID_RE.fullmatch(value) is None:
        raise ValueError(
            "A key id must be 1 to 128 URL-safe base64 characters"
            " (letters, digits, '_', or '-')."
        )

    return value


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Key:
    """Metadata and secret material for one versioned signing key.

    :param secret_key: The HMAC secret key. It is never included in a
        token; only the public :attr:`kid` is emitted.
    :param kid: A stable public key identifier.
    :param can_sign: Whether this key may produce new signatures.
    :param can_verify: Whether this key may verify existing signatures.
    :param expires_at: Optional timezone-aware expiration time.
    :param revoked: Whether the key has been permanently retired.
    """

    secret_key: str | bytes
    kid: str
    can_sign: bool = False
    can_verify: bool = True
    expires_at: datetime | None = None
    revoked: bool = False

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        validate_kid(self.kid)

        if self.expires_at is not None and self.expires_at.tzinfo is None:
            raise ValueError("'expires_at' must be a timezone-aware datetime.")

    @property
    def secret(self) -> bytes:
        return want_bytes(self.secret_key)

    @classmethod
    def signing(
        cls,
        secret_key: str | bytes,
        kid: str,
        expires_at: datetime | None = None,
    ) -> Key:
        """Create a key that may sign and verify."""
        return cls(
            secret_key=secret_key,
            kid=kid,
            can_sign=True,
            can_verify=True,
            expires_at=expires_at,
        )

    @classmethod
    def verification_only(
        cls,
        secret_key: str | bytes,
        kid: str,
        expires_at: datetime | None = None,
        revoked: bool = False,
    ) -> Key:
        """Create a key that may verify but may not produce new tokens."""
        return cls(
            secret_key=secret_key,
            kid=kid,
            can_sign=False,
            can_verify=True,
            expires_at=expires_at,
            revoked=revoked,
        )


class KeyRing:
    """A collection of keys with explicit signing and verification
    lifecycle metadata.
    """

    def __init__(self, keys: cabc.Iterable[Key]):
        keys = tuple(keys)

        if not keys:
            raise ValueError("A key ring must contain at least one key.")

        kids: set[bytes] = set()
        signing_count = 0

        for key in keys:
            kid = validate_kid(key.kid)

            if kid in kids:
                raise ValueError(f"Duplicate key id {key.kid!r}.")

            kids.add(kid)

            if key.can_sign:
                signing_count += 1

        if signing_count != 1:
            raise ValueError("A key ring must have exactly one signing key.")

        self.keys: tuple[Key, ...] = keys
        self._kids = tuple(validate_kid(key.kid) for key in keys)

    @classmethod
    def from_secret_keys(
        cls,
        secret_keys: _SecretKeyInput,
    ) -> KeyRing:
        """Build a ring from the traditional single key or key list.

        The last key is the signing key. Each stable identifier is the
        SHA-256 digest of the corresponding secret material, so reordering
        or removing a verification-only key does not change its ``kid``.
        Explicit :class:`Key` metadata should be used for production
        rotation policies.
        """
        from .signer import _make_keys_list

        raw_keys = _make_keys_list(secret_keys)
        keys = []

        for index, secret in enumerate(raw_keys):
            kid = hashlib.sha256(secret).hexdigest()
            keys.append(
                Key(
                    secret_key=secret,
                    kid=kid,
                    can_sign=index == len(raw_keys) - 1,
                    can_verify=True,
                )
            )

        return cls(keys)

    """Works like the regular :class:`.Signer` but also records the time
    of the signing and can be used to expire signatures. The
    :meth:`unsign` method can raise :exc:`.SignatureExpired` if the
    unsigning failed because the signature is expired.

        """Returns the current timestamp. The function must return an
        integer.
        """
        return int(time.time())

    def timestamp_to_datetime(self, ts: int) -> datetime:
        """Convert the timestamp from :meth:`get_timestamp` into an
        aware :class`datetime.datetime` in UTC.

        .. versionchanged:: 2.0
            The timestamp is returned as a timezone-aware ``datetime``
            in UTC rather than a naive ``datetime`` assumed to be UTC.
        """

    def sign(self, value: str | bytes) -> bytes:
        """Signs the given string and also attaches time information."""
        value = want_bytes(value)
        timestamp = base64_encode(int_to_bytes(self.get_timestamp()))
        sep = want_bytes(self.sep)
        key = self.key_ring.get_signing_key()

    # parameter that affects the return type.

        self,
        signed_value: str | bytes,
        max_age: int | None = None,
        return_timestamp: t.Literal[False] = False,
    ) -> bytes: ...

    def unsign(
        self,
        signed_value: str | bytes,
        max_age: int | None = None,
        return_timestamp: t.Literal[True] = True,
    ) -> tuple[bytes, datetime]: ...

    def unsign(

        return_timestamp: bool = False,
    ) -> tuple[bytes, datetime] | bytes:
        """Works like the regular :meth:`.Signer.unsign` but can also
        validate the time. See the base docstring of the class for
        the general behavior. If ``return_timestamp`` is ``True`` the
        timestamp of the signature will be returned as an aware
        :class:`datetime.datetime` object in UTC.

        .. versionchanged:: 2.0
            The timestamp is returned as a timezone-aware ``datetime``
            in UTC rather than a naive ``datetime`` assumed to be UTC.

        try:
            result = super().unsign(signed_value)
            sig_error = None
        except BadHeader:
            raise
        except BadSignature as e:
            sig_error = e
            result = e.payload or b""

        sep = want_bytes(self.sep)

        # If there is no timestamp in the result there is something
        # seriously wrong. In case there was a signature error, we raise
        # that one directly, otherwise we have a weird situation in
        # which we shouldn't have come except someone uses a time-based
        # serializer on non-timestamp data, so catch that.
        if sep not in result:
            if sig_error:

            if age > max_age:
                raise SignatureExpired(
                    f"Signature age {age} > {max_age} seconds",
                    payload=value,
                    date_signed=self.timestamp_to_datetime(ts_int),

            if age < 0:
                raise SignatureExpired(
                    f"Signature age {age} < 0 seconds",
                    payload=value,
                    date_signed=self.timestamp_to_datetime(ts_int),
                )

        if return_timestamp:
            return value, self.timestamp_to_datetime(ts_int)

        return value

    def validate(self, signed_value: str | bytes, max_age: int | None = None) -> bool:
        """Only validates the given signed value. Returns ``True`` if
        the signature exists and is valid."""

            self.unsign(signed_value, max_age=max_age)

        except BadSignature:

        for index, configured_kid in enumerate(self._kids):
            matched = hmac.compare_digest(kid, configured_kid)
            match_index += (index - match_index) * int(matched)

        return match_index

    def get_signing_key(self, now: datetime | None = None) -> Key:
        for key in self.keys:
            if key.can_sign:
                self._check_status(key, now=now)
                if not key.can_verify:
                    raise KeySigningError(
                        f"Key id {key.kid!r} is not allowed for verification."
                    )
                return key

        # Construction rejects rings without a signing key.
        raise KeySigningError("No signing key is configured.")

    def get_verification_key(
        self, kid: str | bytes, now: datetime | None = None
    ) -> Key:
        if isinstance(kid, str):
            kid = kid.encode("ascii")

        index = self._index_for_kid(kid)

        if index < 0:
            raise UnknownKeyIdentifier(f"Unknown key id {kid!r}.", header=kid)

        key = self.keys[index]
        self._check_status(key, now=now)

        if not key.can_verify:
            raise KeyStatusError(
                f"Key id {key.kid!r} is not allowed for verification.",
                header=kid,
            )

        return key

    def verification_keys(self, now: datetime | None = None) -> cabc.Iterator[Key]:
        for key in self.keys:
            try:
                self._check_status(key, now=now)
            except KeyStatusError:
                continue

            if key.can_verify:
                yield key

    @staticmethod
    def _check_status(key: Key, now: datetime | None = None) -> None:
        if key.revoked:
            raise KeyRevoked(f"Key id {key.kid!r} has been revoked.")

        if key.expires_at is not None:
            current = now or datetime.now(key.expires_at.tzinfo)

            if current >= key.expires_at:
                raise KeyExpired(
                    f"Key id {key.kid!r} expired at {key.expires_at.isoformat()}."
                )

_SecretKeyInput = str | bytes | cabc.Iterable[str] | cabc.Iterable[bytes]
_UNPADDED_BASE64URL_RE = re.compile(rb"[A-Za-z0-9_-]*\Z")
_ENVELOPE_HEADER_RE = re.compile(rb"v1-([A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,128})\Z")


class SigningAlgorithm:
    """Subclasses must implement :meth:`get_signature` to provide
    signature generation functionality.
    """

    def get_signature(self, key: bytes, value: bytes) -> bytes:
        """Returns the signature for the given key and value."""
        raise NotImplementedError()

    def verify_signature(self, key: bytes, value: bytes, sig: bytes) -> bool:
        """Verifies the given signature matches the expected
        signature.
        """
        return hmac.compare_digest(sig, self.get_signature(key, value))


class NoneAlgorithm(SigningAlgorithm):
    """Provides an algorithm that does not perform any signing and
    returns an empty signature.
    """

    def get_signature(self, key: bytes, value: bytes) -> bytes:
        return b""


def _lazy_sha1(string: bytes = b"") -> t.Any:
    """Don't access ``hashlib.sha1`` until runtime. FIPS builds may not include
    SHA-1, in which case the import and use as a default would fail before the
    developer can configure something else.
    """
    return hashlib.sha1(string)


class HMACAlgorithm(SigningAlgorithm):
    """Provides signature generation using HMACs."""

    #: The digest method to use with the MAC algorithm. This defaults to
    #: SHA1, but can be changed to any other function in the hashlib
    #: module.
    default_digest_method: t.Any = staticmethod(_lazy_sha1)

    def __init__(self, digest_method: t.Any = None):
        if digest_method is None:
            digest_method = self.default_digest_method

        self.digest_method: t.Any = digest_method

    def get_signature(self, key: bytes, value: bytes) -> bytes:
        mac = hmac.new(key, msg=value, digestmod=self.digest_method)
        return mac.digest()


def _make_keys_list(
    secret_key: _SecretKeyInput,
) -> list[bytes]:
    if isinstance(secret_key, (str, bytes)):
        return [want_bytes(secret_key)]

    return [want_bytes(s) for s in secret_key]  # pyright: ignore


def _strict_base64_decode(value: bytes) -> bytes:
    """Decode unpadded URL-safe base64 without accepting embedded NUL or
    other non-alphabet characters ignored by the permissive legacy helper.
    """
    if _UNPADDED_BASE64URL_RE.fullmatch(value) is None:
        raise BadSignature(f"Signature {value!r} is not valid base64url")

    return base64_decode(value)


class Signer:
    """A signer securely signs bytes, then unsigns them to verify that
    the value hasn't been changed.

    The secret key should be a random string of ``bytes`` and should not
    be saved to code or version control. Different salts should be used
    to distinguish signing in different contexts. See :doc:`/concepts`
    for information about the security of the secret key and salt.

    :param secret_key: The secret key to sign and verify with. Can be a
        list of keys, oldest to newest, to support key rotation.
    :param salt: Extra key to combine with ``secret_key`` to distinguish
        signatures in different contexts.
    :param sep: Separator between the signature and value.
    :param key_derivation: How to derive the signing key from the secret
        key and salt. Possible values are ``concat``, ``django-concat``,
        or ``hmac``. Defaults to :attr:`default_key_derivation`, which
        defaults to ``django-concat``.
    :param digest_method: Hash function to use when generating the HMAC
        signature. Defaults to :attr:`default_digest_method`, which
        defaults to :func:`hashlib.sha1`. Note that the security of the
        hash alone doesn't apply when used intermediately in HMAC.
    :param algorithm: A :class:`SigningAlgorithm` instance to use
        instead of building a default :class:`HMACAlgorithm` with the
        ``digest_method``.

    .. versionchanged:: 2.0
        Added support for key rotation by passing a list to
        ``secret_key``.

    .. versionchanged:: 0.18
        ``algorithm`` was added as an argument to the class constructor.

    .. versionchanged:: 0.14
        ``key_derivation`` and ``digest_method`` were added as arguments
        to the class constructor.
    """

    #: The default digest method to use for the signer. The default is
    #: :func:`hashlib.sha1`, but can be changed to any :mod:`hashlib` or
    #: compatible object. Note that the security of the hash alone
    #: doesn't apply when used intermediately in HMAC.
    #:
    #: .. versionadded:: 0.14
    default_digest_method: t.Any = staticmethod(_lazy_sha1)

    #: The default scheme to use to derive the signing key from the
    #: secret key and salt. The default is ``django-concat``. Possible
    #: values are ``concat``, ``django-concat``, and ``hmac``.
    #:
    #: .. versionadded:: 0.14
    default_key_derivation: str = "django-concat"

    def __init__(
        self,
        secret_key: _SecretKeyInput | None = None,
        salt: str | bytes | None = b"itsdangerous.Signer",
        sep: str | bytes = b".",
        key_derivation: str | None = None,
        digest_method: t.Any | None = None,
        algorithm: SigningAlgorithm | None = None,
        key_ring: KeyRing | None = None,
    ):
        #: The list of secret keys to try for verifying signatures, from
        #: oldest to newest. The newest (last) key is used for signing.
        #:
        #: This allows a key rotation system to keep a list of allowed
        #: keys and remove expired ones.
        if key_ring is not None and secret_key is not None:
            raise ValueError("Use either 'key_ring' or 'secret_key', not both.")

        if key_ring is None:
            if secret_key is None:
                raise TypeError("A secret key or key ring is required.")

            key_ring = KeyRing.from_secret_keys(secret_key)

        self.key_ring: KeyRing = key_ring
        self.secret_keys: list[bytes] = key_ring.secret_keys
        self.sep: bytes = want_bytes(sep)

        if self.sep in _base64_alphabet:
            raise ValueError(
                "The given separator cannot be used because it may be"
                " contained in the signature itself. ASCII letters,"
                " digits, and '-_=' must not be used."
            )

        if salt is not None:
            salt = want_bytes(salt)
        else:
            salt = b"itsdangerous.Signer"

        self.salt = salt

        if key_derivation is None:
            key_derivation = self.default_key_derivation

        self.key_derivation: str = key_derivation

        if digest_method is None:
            digest_method = self.default_digest_method

        self.digest_method: t.Any = digest_method

        if algorithm is None:
            algorithm = HMACAlgorithm(self.digest_method)

        self.algorithm: SigningAlgorithm = algorithm

    @property
    def secret_key(self) -> bytes:
        """The newest (last) entry in the :attr:`secret_keys` list. This
        is for compatibility from before key rotation support was added.
        """
        return self.secret_keys[-1]

    def derive_key(self, secret_key: str | bytes | None = None) -> bytes:
        """This method is called to derive the key. The default key
        derivation choices can be overridden here. Key derivation is not
        intended to be used as a security method to make a complex key
        out of a short password. Instead you should use large random
        secret keys.

        :param secret_key: A specific secret key to derive from.
            Defaults to the last item in :attr:`secret_keys`.

        .. versionchanged:: 2.0
            Added the ``secret_key`` parameter.
        """
        if secret_key is None:
            secret_key = self.secret_keys[-1]
        else:
            secret_key = want_bytes(secret_key)

        if self.key_derivation == "concat":
            return t.cast(bytes, self.digest_method(self.salt + secret_key).digest())
        elif self.key_derivation == "django-concat":
            return t.cast(
                bytes, self.digest_method(self.salt + b"signer" + secret_key).digest()
            )
        elif self.key_derivation == "hmac":
            mac = hmac.new(secret_key, digestmod=self.digest_method)
            mac.update(self.salt)
            return mac.digest()
        elif self.key_derivation == "none":
            return secret_key
        else:
            raise TypeError("Unknown key derivation method")

    def get_signature(self, value: str | bytes) -> bytes:
        """Returns the signature for the given value."""
        value = want_bytes(value)
        key = self.derive_key(self.key_ring.get_signing_key().secret)
        sig = self.algorithm.get_signature(key, value)
        return base64_encode(sig)

    def _make_envelope_header(self, key_id: bytes) -> bytes:
        return b"v1-" + key_id

    def _parse_envelope_header(self, value: bytes) -> tuple[bytes, bytes] | None:
        """Return ``(header, kid)`` for a syntactically valid v1 envelope.

        The prefix alone is not trusted. A value that merely looks like v1
        still has to authenticate before it is treated as the new format;
        otherwise the legacy parser gets a chance to handle it.
        """
        first_segment, separator, rest = value.partition(self.sep)

        if not separator:
            return None

        match = _ENVELOPE_HEADER_RE.fullmatch(first_segment)

        if match is None:
            return None

        return first_segment, match.group(1)

    def sign(self, value: str | bytes) -> bytes:
        """Signs the given string."""
        value = want_bytes(value)
        key = self.key_ring.get_signing_key()
        header = self._make_envelope_header(key.kid.encode("ascii"))
        signed_value = header + self.sep + value
        return signed_value + self.sep + self.get_signature(signed_value)

    def verify_signature(
        self,
        value: str | bytes,
        sig: str | bytes,
        secret_key: str | bytes | None = None,
    ) -> bool:
        """Verifies the signature for the given value."""
        try:
            sig = _strict_base64_decode(want_bytes(sig))
        except Exception:
            return False

        value = want_bytes(value)

        if secret_key is None:
            secret_keys = list(self.secret_keys)
        else:
            secret_keys = [want_bytes(secret_key)]

        # Constant-time MAC comparison happens in the algorithm. Iterate in
        # reverse to preserve the newest-to-oldest legacy verification order.
        for candidate in reversed(secret_keys):
            key = self.derive_key(candidate)

            if self.algorithm.verify_signature(key, value, sig):
                return True

        return False

    def _verify_legacy_signature_at(
        self, value: bytes, sig: bytes, current_time: datetime
    ) -> bool:
        for key in self.key_ring.verification_keys(now=current_time):
            if self.verify_signature(value, sig, key.secret):
                return True

        return False

    def _verify_legacy_signature(self, value: bytes, sig: bytes) -> bool:
        return self._verify_legacy_signature_at(value, sig, datetime.now(timezone.utc))

    def _unsign_versioned(self, value: bytes, sig: bytes, payload: bytes) -> bytes:
        parsed = self._parse_envelope_header(value)

        if parsed is None:
            raise BadSignature(f"Signature {sig!r} does not match", payload=payload)

        header, kid = parsed
        current_time = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

        try:
            key = self.key_ring.get_verification_key(kid, now=current_time)
        except KeyStatusError as err:
            # A revoked/expired candidate must not be silently accepted as a
            # similarly prefixed legacy token. Unknown/malformed ids still
            # preserve the legacy compatibility path below.
            err.payload = payload
            raise
        except BadHeader:
            if self._verify_legacy_signature_at(value, sig, current_time):
                return value

            raise

        if not self.verify_signature(value, sig, key.secret):
            raise BadSignature(f"Signature {sig!r} does not match", payload=payload)

        return payload

    def unsign(self, signed_value: str | bytes) -> bytes:
        """Unsigns the given string."""
        signed_value = want_bytes(signed_value)

        if self.sep not in signed_value:
            raise BadSignature(f"No {self.sep!r} found in value")

        value, sig = signed_value.rsplit(self.sep, 1)

        if self._parse_envelope_header(value) is not None:
            _header, *payload_parts = value.split(self.sep)
            payload = self.sep.join(payload_parts)

            try:
                return self._unsign_versioned(value, sig, payload)
            except BadHeader:
                raise
            except BadSignature as err:
                # Only syntactically valid v1 candidates reach this path.
                # Their explicit prefix is an authenticated format selector,
                # so a failed MAC must not be retried under the old format.
                raise err

        if self._verify_legacy_signature_at(value, sig, datetime.now(timezone.utc)):
            return value

        raise BadSignature(f"Signature {sig!r} does not match", payload=value)

    def validate(self, signed_value: str | bytes) -> bool:
        """Only validates the given signed value. Returns ``True`` if
        the signature exists and is valid.
        """
        try:
            self.unsign(signed_value)
            return True
        except BadSignature:
            return False

class TimestampSigner(Signer):
    """Works like the regular :class:`.Signer` but also records the time
    of the signing and can be used to expire signatures. The
    :meth:`unsign` method can raise :exc:`.SignatureExpired` if the
    unsigning failed because the signature is expired.
    """

    def get_timestamp(self) -> int:
        """Returns the current timestamp. The function must return an
        integer.
        """
        return int(time.time())

    def timestamp_to_datetime(self, ts: int) -> datetime:
        """Convert the timestamp from :meth:`get_timestamp` into an
        aware :class`datetime.datetime` in UTC.

        .. versionchanged:: 2.0
            The timestamp is returned as a timezone-aware ``datetime``
            in UTC rather than a naive ``datetime`` assumed to be UTC.
        """
        return datetime.fromtimestamp(ts, tz=timezone.utc)

    def sign(self, value: str | bytes) -> bytes:
        """Signs the given string and also attaches time information."""
        value = want_bytes(value)
        timestamp = base64_encode(int_to_bytes(self.get_timestamp()))
        sep = want_bytes(self.sep)
        key = self.key_ring.get_signing_key()
        header = self._make_envelope_header(key.kid.encode("ascii"))
        value = header + sep + value + sep + timestamp
        return value + sep + self.get_signature(value)

    # Ignore overlapping signatures check, return_timestamp is the only
    # parameter that affects the return type.

    @t.overload
    def unsign(  # pyright: ignore
        self,
        signed_value: str | bytes,
        max_age: int | None = None,
        return_timestamp: t.Literal[False] = False,
    ) -> bytes: ...

    @t.overload
    def unsign(
        self,
        signed_value: str | bytes,
        max_age: int | None = None,
        return_timestamp: t.Literal[True] = True,
    ) -> tuple[bytes, datetime]: ...

    def unsign(
        self,
        signed_value: str | bytes,
        max_age: int | None = None,
        return_timestamp: bool = False,
    ) -> tuple[bytes, datetime] | bytes:
        """Works like the regular :meth:`.Signer.unsign` but can also
        validate the time. See the base docstring of the class for
        the general behavior. If ``return_timestamp`` is ``True`` the
        timestamp of the signature will be returned as an aware
        :class:`datetime.datetime` object in UTC.

        .. versionchanged:: 2.0
            The timestamp is returned as a timezone-aware ``datetime``
            in UTC rather than a naive ``datetime`` assumed to be UTC.
        """
        try:
            result = super().unsign(signed_value)
            sig_error = None
        except BadHeader:
            raise
        except BadSignature as e:
            sig_error = e
            result = e.payload or b""

        sep = want_bytes(self.sep)

        # If there is no timestamp in the result there is something
        # seriously wrong. In case there was a signature error, we raise
        # that one directly, otherwise we have a weird situation in
        # which we shouldn't have come except someone uses a time-based
        # serializer on non-timestamp data, so catch that.
        if sep not in result:
            if sig_error:
                raise sig_error

            raise BadTimeSignature("timestamp missing", payload=result)

        value, ts_bytes = result.rsplit(sep, 1)
        ts_int: int | None = None
        ts_dt: datetime | None = None

        try:
            ts_int = bytes_to_int(base64_decode(ts_bytes))
        except Exception:
            pass

        # Signature is *not* okay. Raise a proper error now that we have
        # split the value and the timestamp.
        if sig_error is not None:
            if ts_int is not None:
                try:
                    ts_dt = self.timestamp_to_datetime(ts_int)
                except (ValueError, OSError, OverflowError) as exc:
                    # Windows raises OSError
                    # 32-bit raises OverflowError
                    raise BadTimeSignature(
                        "Malformed timestamp", payload=value
                    ) from exc

            raise BadTimeSignature(str(sig_error), payload=value, date_signed=ts_dt)

        # Signature was okay but the timestamp is actually not there or
        # malformed. Should not happen, but we handle it anyway.
        if ts_int is None:
            raise BadTimeSignature("Malformed timestamp", payload=value)

        # Check timestamp is not older than max_age
        if max_age is not None:
            age = self.get_timestamp() - ts_int

            if age > max_age:
                raise SignatureExpired(
                    f"Signature age {age} > {max_age} seconds",
                    payload=value,
                    date_signed=self.timestamp_to_datetime(ts_int),
                )

            if age < 0:
                raise SignatureExpired(
                    f"Signature age {age} < 0 seconds",
                    payload=value,
                    date_signed=self.timestamp_to_datetime(ts_int),
                )

        if return_timestamp:
            return value, self.timestamp_to_datetime(ts_int)

        return value

    def validate(self, signed_value: str | bytes, max_age: int | None = None) -> bool:
        """Only validates the given signed value. Returns ``True`` if
        the signature exists and is valid."""
        try:
            self.unsign(signed_value, max_age=max_age)
            return True
        except BadSignature:
            return False

    """Uses :class:`TimestampSigner` instead of the default
    :class:`.Signer`.
    """

    default_signer: type[TimestampSigner] = TimestampSigner  # pyright: ignore

Key Rotation
------------

Key rotation can provide an extra layer of mitigation against an
attacker discovering a secret key. A rotation system will keep a list of
valid keys, generating a new key and removing the oldest key
periodically. If it takes four weeks for an attacker to crack a key, but
the key is rotated out after three weeks, they will not be able to use
any keys they crack. However, if a user doesn't refresh their token
within three weeks it will be invalid too.

The system that generates and maintains keys is outside the scope of
ItsDangerous, but the library now supports explicit key lifecycle metadata
through :class:`Key` and :class:`KeyRing`.

Version 1 envelopes use this layout::

    v1-<kid>.<payload>[.<timestamp>].<signature>

``kid`` is public and limited to the unpadded URL-safe base64 alphabet, so
it cannot contain the envelope separator. The HMAC input is the complete
value before the final signature, including ``v1`` and ``kid``. Changing
the version or key identifier therefore changes the bytes that the MAC
covers and causes verification to fail. This prevents an attacker from
downgrading an envelope or moving a valid signature onto another key.

The HMAC itself remains the format and key-selection authority. A token
without a syntactically valid version-1 header is handled by the legacy
parser. A token that merely looks like version 1 still has to authenticate
before the version-1 path accepts it, which keeps legacy payloads that may
contain dots from being misclassified.

Configure one key with ``can_sign=True``. Retired keys remain available for
verification only, optionally with an expiration time or a revocation flag.

.. code-block:: python

    from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
    from itsdangerous import Key, KeyRing, URLSafeTimedSerializer

    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    ring = KeyRing([
        Key.verification_only(previous_key, "2026-a", expires_at=now + timedelta(days=30)),
        Key.signing(current_key, "2026-b"),
    ])
    serializer = URLSafeTimedSerializer(key_ring=ring)

To add a key, keep the current key as verification-only and add the new key
with signing enabled. To terminate a retired key before its natural cutoff,
set ``revoked=True`` or remove it from the ring. Removing a key rejects
future verification for all tokens carrying that ``kid``; revocation gives
you a distinct :exc:`~itsdangerous.exc.KeyRevoked` exception for audit
logging. An expired key raises
:exc:`~itsdangerous.exc.KeyExpired`, while a ``kid`` that is not configured
raises :exc:`~itsdangerous.exc.UnknownKeyIdentifier`.

The traditional single-key and key-list constructors remain supported. They
generate a stable SHA-256-based ``kid`` for each key, use the last key for
signing, and retain the legacy verification path for tokens created before
this feature.

from __future__ import annotations

import typing as t
from datetime import datetime


class BadData(Exception):
    """Raised if bad data of any sort was encountered. This is the base
    for all exceptions that ItsDangerous defines.

    .. versionadded:: 0.15
    """

    def __init__(self, message: str):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.message = message

    def __str__(self) -> str:
        return self.message


class BadSignature(BadData):
    """Raised if a signature does not match."""

    def __init__(self, message: str, payload: t.Any | None = None):
        super().__init__(message)

        #: The payload that failed the signature test. In some
        #: situations you might still want to inspect this, even if
        #: you know it was tampered with.
        #:
        #: .. versionadded:: 0.14

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from datetime import datetime
from datetime import timedelta
from datetime import timezone

import pytest
from freezegun import freeze_time

from itsdangerous import BadHeader
from itsdangerous import BadKeyIdentifier
from itsdangerous import BadSignature
from itsdangerous import Key
from itsdangerous import KeyExpired
from itsdangerous import KeyRevoked
from itsdangerous import KeyRing
from itsdangerous import Signer
from itsdangerous import TimestampSigner
from itsdangerous import UnknownKeyIdentifier
from itsdangerous import URLSafeTimedSerializer
from itsdangerous.encoding import base64_encode


def make_secret() -> bytes:
    return os.urandom(32)


def make_ring(*, revoked: bool = False) -> KeyRing:
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    return KeyRing(
        [
            Key.verification_only(
                make_secret(),
                "old",
                expires_at=now + timedelta(days=30),
                revoked=revoked,
            ),
            Key.signing(make_secret(), "current"),
        ]
    )


class TestVersionedEnvelope:
    def test_signer_round_trip_and_header(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        signer = Signer(key_ring=ring)

        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")

        assert signed.startswith(b"v1-current.")
        assert signer.unsign(signed) == b"payload"

    def test_timestamped_round_trip(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        signer = TimestampSigner(key_ring=ring)
        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")

        assert signed.startswith(b"v1-current.")
        assert signer.unsign(signed, max_age=10) == b"payload"

    def test_legacy_timestamped_token_remains_valid(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        old_signer = TimestampSigner(ring.secret_keys)
        old_signed = self._legacy_timestamp_sign(old_signer, b"payload")

        assert not old_signed.startswith(b"v1-")
        assert (
            TimestampSigner(key_ring=ring).unsign(old_signed, max_age=10) == b"payload"
        )

    def test_url_safe_full_stack_with_compression_and_max_age(self):
        serializer = URLSafeTimedSerializer(key_ring=make_ring())
        value = {"message": "x" * 1000}
        token = serializer.dumps(value)

        assert token.startswith("v1-current.")
        assert all(char.isascii() and char not in "?#" for char in token)
        assert serializer.loads(token, max_age=10) == value

    def test_kid_selects_exact_key(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        signer = Signer(key_ring=ring)
        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")
        original_signer = signer

        class OneKeyAlgorithm:
            calls = 0

            def get_signature(self, key, value):
                self.calls += 1
                return original_signer.algorithm.get_signature(key, value)

            def verify_signature(self, key, value, sig):
                self.calls += 1
                return original_signer.algorithm.verify_signature(key, value, sig)

        algorithm = OneKeyAlgorithm()
        verifier = Signer(key_ring=ring, algorithm=algorithm)

        assert verifier.unsign(signed) == b"payload"

        assert algorithm.calls == 1

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("position", (0, 1))
    def test_tampered_kid_fails(self, position):
        signer = Signer(key_ring=make_ring())
        signed = bytearray(signer.sign(b"payload"))
        signed[position] = ord("x")

        with pytest.raises((BadHeader, BadSignature)):
            signer.unsign(bytes(signed))

    def test_version_downgrade_fails(self):
        signer = Signer(key_ring=make_ring())
        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")
        downgraded = signed.replace(b"v1-", b"v0-", 1)

        with pytest.raises(BadHeader):
            signer.unsign(downgraded)

    def test_unsupported_version_is_header_error(self):
        signer = Signer(key_ring=make_ring())

        with pytest.raises(BadHeader):
            signer.unsign(b"v2-current.payload.sig")

    def test_unknown_kid_is_header_error(self):
        signer = Signer(key_ring=make_ring())
        signed = signer.sign(b"payload").replace(b"v1-current", b"v1-missing", 1)

        with pytest.raises(UnknownKeyIdentifier) as exc_info:
            signer.unsign(signed)

        assert isinstance(exc_info.value, BadHeader)

    def test_malformed_kid_is_header_error(self):
        signer = Signer(key_ring=make_ring())
        token = signer.sign(b"payload")
        value, sig = token.rsplit(b".", 1)
        malformed = value.replace(b"v1-current", b"v1-bad kid", 1) + b"." + sig

        with pytest.raises(BadSignature):
            signer.unsign(malformed)

    def test_malformed_versioned_header_is_not_ambiguous(self):
        signer = Signer(key_ring=make_ring())

        with pytest.raises(BadKeyIdentifier):
            signer.unsign(b"v1-.payload.sig")

    def test_empty_kid_with_nested_separator_is_rejected(self):
        signer = Signer(key_ring=make_ring())

        with pytest.raises(BadKeyIdentifier):
            signer.unsign(b"v1-.extra.payload.sig")

    def test_invalid_signature_encoding(self):
        signer = Signer(key_ring=make_ring())
        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")
        value, _sig = signed.rsplit(b".", 1)

        for invalid_sig in (b"bad/sig", b"bad=sig"):
            with pytest.raises(BadSignature):
                signer.unsign(value + b"." + invalid_sig)

    def test_kid_cannot_contain_separator(self):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            Key(make_secret(), "bad.kid")

    def test_legacy_token_remains_valid(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        old_signer = Signer(ring.secret_keys)
        old_signed = self._legacy_sign(old_signer, b"payload")

        assert not old_signed.startswith(b"v1-")
        assert Signer(key_ring=ring).unsign(old_signed) == b"payload"

    def test_legacy_looking_token_is_not_confused_with_new_format(self):
        ring = make_ring()

        assert Signer(key_ring=ring).unsign(old_signed) == old_payload

    @staticmethod
    def _legacy_sign(signer: Signer, value: bytes) -> bytes:
        key = signer.derive_key(signer.secret_keys[-1])
        signature = signer.algorithm.get_signature(key, value)

        return value + signer.sep + base64_encode(signature)

    @staticmethod
    def _legacy_timestamp_sign(signer: TimestampSigner, value: bytes) -> bytes:
        from itsdangerous.encoding import int_to_bytes

        timestamp = base64_encode(int_to_bytes(signer.get_timestamp()))
        timed_value = value + signer.sep + timestamp
        key = signer.derive_key(signer.secret_keys[-1])
        signature = signer.algorithm.get_signature(key, timed_value)

        return timed_value + signer.sep + base64_encode(signature)

        ring = KeyRing(

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from datetime import datetime
from datetime import timedelta
from datetime import timezone

import pytest
from freezegun import freeze_time

from itsdangerous import BadHeader
from itsdangerous import BadKeyIdentifier
from itsdangerous import BadSignature
from itsdangerous import Key
from itsdangerous import KeyExpired
from itsdangerous import KeyRevoked
from itsdangerous import KeyRing
from itsdangerous import Signer
from itsdangerous import TimestampSigner
from itsdangerous import UnknownKeyIdentifier
from itsdangerous import URLSafeTimedSerializer
from itsdangerous.encoding import base64_encode


def make_secret() -> bytes:
    return os.urandom(32)


def make_ring(*, revoked: bool = False) -> KeyRing:
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    return KeyRing(
        [
            Key.verification_only(
                make_secret(),
                "old",
                expires_at=now + timedelta(days=30),
                revoked=revoked,
            ),
            Key.signing(make_secret(), "current"),
        ]
    )


class TestVersionedEnvelope:
    def test_signer_round_trip_and_header(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        signer = Signer(key_ring=ring)

        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")

        assert signed.startswith(b"v1-current.")
        assert signer.unsign(signed) == b"payload"

    def test_timestamped_round_trip(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        signer = TimestampSigner(key_ring=ring)
        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")

        assert signed.startswith(b"v1-current.")
        assert signer.unsign(signed, max_age=10) == b"payload"

    def test_legacy_timestamped_token_remains_valid(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        old_signer = TimestampSigner(ring.secret_keys)
        old_signed = self._legacy_timestamp_sign(old_signer, b"payload")

        assert not old_signed.startswith(b"v1-")
        assert (
            TimestampSigner(key_ring=ring).unsign(old_signed, max_age=10) == b"payload"
        )

    def test_url_safe_full_stack_with_compression_and_max_age(self):
        serializer = URLSafeTimedSerializer(key_ring=make_ring())
        value = {"message": "x" * 1000}
        token = serializer.dumps(value)

        assert token.startswith("v1-current.")
        assert all(char.isascii() and char not in "?#" for char in token)
        assert serializer.loads(token, max_age=10) == value

    def test_kid_selects_exact_key(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        signer = Signer(key_ring=ring)
        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")
        original_signer = signer

        class OneKeyAlgorithm:
            calls = 0

            def get_signature(self, key, value):
                self.calls += 1
                return original_signer.algorithm.get_signature(key, value)

            def verify_signature(self, key, value, sig):
                self.calls += 1
                return original_signer.algorithm.verify_signature(key, value, sig)

        algorithm = OneKeyAlgorithm()
        verifier = Signer(key_ring=ring, algorithm=algorithm)

        assert verifier.unsign(signed) == b"payload"

        assert algorithm.calls == 1

    @pytest.mark.parametrize("position", (0, 1))
    def test_tampered_kid_fails(self, position):
        signer = Signer(key_ring=make_ring())
        signed = bytearray(signer.sign(b"payload"))
        signed[position] = ord("x")

        with pytest.raises((BadHeader, BadSignature)):
            signer.unsign(bytes(signed))

    def test_version_downgrade_fails(self):
        signer = Signer(key_ring=make_ring())
        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")
        downgraded = signed.replace(b"v1-", b"v0-", 1)

        with pytest.raises(BadHeader):
            signer.unsign(downgraded)

    def test_unsupported_version_is_header_error(self):
        signer = Signer(key_ring=make_ring())

    def test_unknown_kid_is_header_error(self):

        with pytest.raises(UnknownKeyIdentifier) as exc_info:

        for invalid_sig in (b"bad/sig", b"bad=sig"):

                signer.unsign(value + b"." + invalid_sig)

    def test_kid_cannot_contain_separator(self):

    def _legacy_sign(signer: Signer, value: bytes) -> bytes:
        key = signer.derive_key(signer.secret_keys[-1])
        signature = signer.algorithm.get_signature(key, value)

        return value + signer.sep + base64_encode(signature)

from __future__ import annotations

import os
from datetime import datetime
from datetime import timedelta
from datetime import timezone

import pytest
from freezegun import freeze_time

from itsdangerous import BadHeader
from itsdangerous import BadKeyIdentifier
from itsdangerous import BadSignature
from itsdangerous import Key
from itsdangerous import KeyExpired
from itsdangerous import KeyRevoked
from itsdangerous import KeyRing
from itsdangerous import Signer
from itsdangerous import TimestampSigner
from itsdangerous import UnknownKeyIdentifier
from itsdangerous import URLSafeTimedSerializer
from itsdangerous.encoding import base64_encode
from itsdangerous.encoding import int_to_bytes


def make_secret() -> bytes:
    return os.urandom(32)


def make_ring(*, revoked: bool = False) -> KeyRing:
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    return KeyRing(
        [
            Key.verification_only(
                make_secret(),
                "old",
                expires_at=now + timedelta(days=30),
                revoked=revoked,
            ),
            Key.signing(make_secret(), "current"),
        ]
    )


def test_duplicate_traditional_secret_keys_are_deduplicated():
    secret = make_secret()
    ring = KeyRing.from_secret_keys([secret, secret])

    assert ring.secret_keys == [secret]


class TestVersionedEnvelope:
    def test_signer_round_trip_and_header(self):
        ring = make_ring()
        signer = Signer(key_ring=ring)

        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")

        assert signed.startswith(b"v1-current.")
        assert signer.unsign(signed) == b"payload"
    @classmethod
    def from_secret_keys(
        cls,
        secret_keys: _SecretKeyInput,
    ) -> KeyRing:
        """Build a ring from the traditional single key or key list.

        The last key is the signing key. Each stable identifier is the
        SHA-256 digest of the corresponding secret material, so reordering
        or removing a verification-only key does not change its ``kid``.
        Duplicate secret material is ignored to preserve unique identifiers.
        Explicit :class:`Key` metadata should be used for production
        rotation policies.
        """
        from .signer import _make_keys_list

        raw_keys = _make_keys_list(secret_keys)
        unique_raw_keys: list[bytes] = []
        keys = []

        for secret in raw_keys:
            if secret not in unique_raw_keys:
                unique_raw_keys.append(secret)

        for index, secret in enumerate(unique_raw_keys):
            kid = hashlib.sha256(secret).hexdigest()
            keys.append(
                Key(
                    secret_key=secret,
                    kid=kid,
                    can_sign=index == len(unique_raw_keys) - 1,
                    can_verify=True,

import os

from datetime import timezone

from itsdangerous import BadKeyIdentifier

from itsdangerous import TimestampSigner

from itsdangerous.encoding import base64_encode
from itsdangerous.encoding import int_to_bytes


def make_secret() -> bytes:
    return os.urandom(32)


def make_ring(*, revoked: bool = False) -> KeyRing:
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
    return KeyRing(
        [
            Key.verification_only(
                make_secret(),
                "old",
                expires_at=now + timedelta(days=30),
                revoked=revoked,
            ),
            Key.signing(make_secret(), "current"),
        ]
    )


def test_duplicate_traditional_secret_keys_are_deduplicated():

        ring = make_ring()
        signer = Signer(key_ring=ring)

        signed = signer.sign(b"payload")

        assert signed.startswith(b"v1-current.")
        assert signer.unsign(signed) == b"payload"
    @classmethod
    def from_secret_keys(
        cls,
        secret_keys: _SecretKeyInput,
    ) -> KeyRing:
        """Build a ring from the traditional single key or key list.

        The last key is the signing key. Each stable identifier is the
        SHA-256 digest of the corresponding secret material, so reordering
        or removing a verification-only key does not change its ``kid``.
        Duplicate secret material is ignored to preserve unique identifiers.
        Explicit :class:`Key` metadata should be used for production
        rotation policies.
        """
        from .signer import _make_keys_list

        raw_keys = _make_keys_list(secret_keys)
        unique_raw_keys: list[bytes] = []
        keys = []

        for secret in raw_keys:
            if secret not in unique_raw_keys:
                unique_raw_keys.append(secret)

        for index, secret in enumerate(unique_raw_keys):
            kid = hashlib.sha256(secret).hexdigest()
            keys.append(
                Key(
                    secret_key=secret,
                    kid=kid,
                    can_sign=index == len(unique_raw_keys) - 1,
                    can_verify=True,
                )
            )

        return cls(keys)

    @property
    def secret_keys(self) -> list[bytes]:
        return [key.secret for key in self.keys]
